There are few people who have shaped the story of New Zealand cinema as profoundly as Sir Sam Neill.
 
From his breakout role in Sleeping Dogs, to the haunting beauty of The Piano, and later as the beloved Hector in Hunt for the Wilderpeople, Sam helped define how New Zealand sees itself on screen.
 
His international career was just as extraordinary. As Dr Alan Grant in Jurassic Park, he inspired a generation of aspiring palaeontologists and showed New Zealanders you could have a career that took you around the world while remaining strongly connected to home.
 
Beyond the screen, he was admired for his warmth, generosity, sharp wit and deep love for this country, its people and Pinot Noir.
 
Sam’s work will continue to be watched, celebrated and discovered by audiences for generations to come.
 
Our thoughts are with Sam's whānau, friends, colleagues and all those who had the privilege of knowing and working with him.","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nzfilm_sam-neill-nzfc-activity-7482325157122904064-qrWJ"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"New Zealand Film Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/nzfilm"},"datePublished":"2026-07-06T22:58:49.488Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nzfilm_nzfilm-screenindustry-filmfunding-activity-7480032538686689280--QBD","text":"Got questions about NZFC funding? 📅 Online, Thursday 16th July, 12 pm - 1:30 pm
🔗 Register now: https://lnkd.in/eZTzA7jS
📸 Photo by Dean MacKenzie, BTS of Holy Days (2026) 

We look forward to connecting with filmmakers from across Aotearoa.

Animator Eden Laing (Mukpuddy Ltd) shares a chance encounter in Annecy that turned into a meaningful industry connection.

These moments, outside formal meetings and events, are part of what makes being on the ground at international markets so valuable, creating space for unexpected conversations and future opportunities.

NZFC is proud to support New Zealand creatives as they connect and share their work internationally.

Annie Murray Chris Payne Bevin Linkhorn | Festival international du film d'animation d'Annecy | #NZFilm #AnimationIndustry #Annecy2026 #ScreenIndustry #AnnecyMIFA #GlobalStorytelling","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nzfilm_nzfilm-animationindustry-annecy2026-activity-7476710951266746368-b9mm"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"New Zealand Film Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/nzfilm"},"datePublished":"2026-06-27T05:00:05.873Z","headline":"","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nzfilm_nzfilm-animationindustry-annecy2026-activity-7476499577454551040-Ar8x","text":"Why Annecy matters for the animation sector

Founder and Creative Director of 37Degrees Studio, Marie Tricart, reflects on the value of Annecy as a global meeting point for animation, bringing together established creatives, emerging talent and industry leaders.

For New Zealand creatives, it provides an important opportunity to reconnect with collaborators, build new relationships and stay across how the industry is evolving internationally.

NZFC is proud to support this continued engagement between Aotearoa and the global animation community.

Marie Tricart 🔜 Annecy, MIFA | Annie Murray Chris Payne Bevin Linkhorn | 37Degrees Studio | Festival international du film d'animation d'Annecy |#NZFilm #AnimationIndustry #Annecy2026 #ScreenIndustry #AnnecyMIFA #GlobalStorytelling","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nzfilm_nzfilm-animationindustry-annecy2026-activity-7476499577454551040-Ar8x"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"New Zealand Film Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/nzfilm"},"datePublished":"2026-06-26T22:21:17.133Z","headline":"","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nzfilm_nzfilm-animationindustry-annecy2026-activity-7476399213095026688-D6pQ","text":"NZFC at Annecy: supporting New Zealand animation

NZFC CEO Annie Murray shares what it means to be on the ground at Annecy MIFA, the world’s largest animation market, supporting producers to connect with the partners they need to bring projects to life.

From the NZFC booth to celebrating films in the programme, including the short film Grounded, and the premiere of the feature Kiri and Lou Go Raaa!, Annecy provides a key platform for showcasing New Zealand animation and strengthening international relationships.

Annie Murray Chris Payne Bevin Linkhorn Fiona Copland | Wētā FX Festival international du film d'animation d'Annecy | #NZFilm #AnimationIndustry #Annecy2026 #ScreenIndustry #AnnecyMIFA #GlobalStorytelling","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nzfilm_nzfilm-animationindustry-annecy2026-activity-7476399213095026688-D6pQ"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"New Zealand Film Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/nzfilm"},"datePublished":"2026-06-26T05:00:52.108Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nzfilm_annecy-mifa-2026-nzfc-activity-7476137383466512384-J0zy","text":"NZFC is on the ground in Annecy with CEO Annie Murray, Deputy CEO and Head of Co‑Production and Incentives Chris Payne, and Investment & Development Executive Bevin Linkhorn. 
 
Highlights from the day included a Wētā FX takeover of the NZFC booth, led by Sidney Kombo‑Kintombo, as well as engagement with international partners such as Telefilm Canada and Ontario Creates. 
 
These conversations support project development, strengthen partnerships, and help open pathways for New Zealand animation in the global market. 
 
Annie Murray Chris Payne Bevin Linkhorn Sidney Kombo-Kintombo Fiona Copland | Wētā FX Telefilm Canada Ontario Creates Festival international du film d'animation d'Annecy | #NZFilm #AnimationIndustry #Annecy2026 #ScreenIndustry #AnnecyMIFA  #GlobalStorytelling ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nzfilm_annecy-mifa-2026-nzfc-activity-7476137383466512384-J0zy"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"New Zealand Film Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/nzfilm"},"datePublished":"2026-06-25T19:00:06.408Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nzfilm_grounded-in-annecy-june-2026-nzfc-activity-7475986196855328769-mzzs","text":"Celebrating Grounded at Annecy 🐞

NZFC is pleased to support Grounded and the team behind the film — including filmmakers Adam Reynolds and Chris Callus — as it screens at Annecy.

Originally created in a single weekend for the Vista Foundation 48Hours competition, the short film went on to be named Grand Champion, selected by an international jury including Sir Peter Jackson, Elijah Wood and Dame Gaylene Preston.

Since then, the team has thoughtfully evolved the film’s visual language while retaining its core story - dialogue‑free exploration of feeling stuck and the quiet power of emotional support.

Congratulations to Adam, Chris and the wider team on this continued momentum and international recognition. We’re proud to be on the ground continuing our support of Grounded in Annecy.
 
Annie Murray Chris Payne Bevin Linkhorn Adam Reynolds Chris Callus | Festival international du film d'animation d'Annecy | #NZFilm #AnimationIndustry #Annecy2026 #ScreenIndustry #AnnecyMIFA  #GlobalStorytelling ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nzfilm_grounded-in-annecy-june-2026-nzfc-activity-7475986196855328769-mzzs"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"New Zealand Film Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/nzfilm"},"datePublished":"2026-06-25T05:00:07.179Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nzfilm_nzfc-in-annecy-mifa-june-2026-nzfc-activity-7475774807163359234-569F","text":"NZFC is attending the Annecy International Animation Film Festival with CEO Annie Murray, Deputy CEO and Head of Co‑Production and Incentives Chris Payne, and Investment & Development Executive Bevin Linkhorn, alongside a strong New Zealand delegation. 
 
In the first days of the festival, the team has engaged in a range of activities, including hosting the Kiwi welcome event, participating in Co‑Create at MIFA, and holding meetings with international partners across Japan, Ireland, Taiwan and other key markets to support collaboration and project development. 
 
Annecy MIFA provides a key global platform for New Zealand to connect with partners, progress projects and showcase the strength of our animation sector. 
 
NZFC has also supported New Zealand work on screen, including Grounded and Kiri and Lou Go Raaa!, and celebrated Kiwi talent across the programme, including Wētā FX’s Sidney Kombo-Kintombo. 
 
More to follow as the week continues.

We support talented filmmakers to develop their careers, foster international partnerships, and grow global audiences for New Zealand films. Our work includes marketing New Zealand’s screen production industry internationally, attracting overseas productions, and providing expert advice as the first point of contact for incoming projects.

  <div class="attributed-text-segment-list__container relative mt-1 mb-1.5 babybear:mt-0 babybear:mb-0.5">
    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Kua hinga tētahi tōtara i Te Waonui-a-Tāne.
 
There are few people who have shaped the story of New Zealand cinema as profoundly as Sir Sam Neill.
 
From his breakout role in Sleeping Dogs, to the haunting beauty of The Piano, and later as the beloved Hector in Hunt for the Wilderpeople, Sam helped define how New Zealand sees itself on screen.
 
His international career was just as extraordinary. As Dr Alan Grant in Jurassic Park, he inspired a generation of aspiring palaeontologists and showed New Zealanders you could have a career that took you around the world while remaining strongly connected to home.
 
Beyond the screen, he was admired for his warmth, generosity, sharp wit and deep love for this country, its people and Pinot Noir.
 
Sam’s work will continue to be watched, celebrated and discovered by audiences for generations to come.
 
Our thoughts are with Sam's whānau, friends, colleagues and all those who had the privilege of knowing and working with him.</p>

Made with funding from the Lottery Grants Board via <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/nzfilm?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>New Zealand Film Commission</a>, the film tells the story of <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/darren-pene-pati-2ab8a97a?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Darren Pene Pati</a> and his brother <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/amitai-pati-85461484?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Amitai Pati</a>, and their journey from Samoa, to platinum selling success in the trio Sol3 Mio, and the world's great opera stages. 
It has struck a powerful chord with audiences, reaching number one at the New Zealand box office after opening in March and going on to become one of Aotearoa’s most successful local documentaries.
Rebecca’s richly detailed storytelling brought the journey to life for our team, from the years of work behind the film to the craft, care and commitment that went into sharing this remarkable story.
Congratulations to Rebecca and everyone involved in this extraordinary film – we can’t wait to see where their stories take them next.
'Tenor: My Name is Pati' is still playing in selected cinemas around the country – get a ticket while you still can!

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Celebrating Grounded at Annecy 🐞

NZFC is pleased to support Grounded and the team behind the film — including filmmakers Adam Reynolds and Chris Callus — as it screens at Annecy.

Originally created in a single weekend for the <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/vista-foundation?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Vista Foundation</a> 48Hours competition, the short film went on to be named Grand Champion, selected by an international jury including Sir Peter Jackson, Elijah Wood and Dame <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/gaylene-preston-13026418?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Gaylene Preston</a>.

Since then, the team has thoughtfully evolved the film’s visual language while retaining its core story - dialogue‑free exploration of feeling stuck and the quiet power of emotional support.

Congratulations to Adam, Chris and the wider team on this continued momentum and international recognition. We’re proud to be on the ground continuing our support of Grounded in Annecy.

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">NZFC is attending the Annecy International Animation Film Festival with CEO Annie Murray, Deputy CEO and Head of Co‑Production and Incentives Chris Payne, and Investment & Development Executive Bevin Linkhorn, alongside a strong New Zealand delegation. 
 
In the first days of the festival, the team has engaged in a range of activities, including hosting the Kiwi welcome event, participating in Co‑Create at MIFA, and holding meetings with international partners across Japan, Ireland, Taiwan and other key markets to support collaboration and project development. 
 
Annecy MIFA provides a key global platform for New Zealand to connect with partners, progress projects and showcase the strength of our animation sector.
